sharedText: of the Lord: and as many
reason: A six-word run straddling a clause boundary, made of an attribution formula and a quantifier. The association is tempting for a better reason than the wording — Acts 13:46-48 is Paul turning from the Jews to the Gentiles, which is 30:2's subject exactly — but Acts's 'as many as were ordained to eternal life believed' is a statement about election and 30:2's 'as many of the Gentiles as will repent' is a statement about condition. Nothing verbal survives the comparison. Registered rather than passed over because the thematic pull is real and a careful reader might accept it on that pull alone.

'The Holy One of Israel' is the Book of Mormon's standing title for Christ and occurs in some thirty KJV verses, most of them in Isaiah. Isaiah 12:6 is one of them and is also transcribed in this book at 2 Nephi 22:6, which is why the stream ranked it; neither fact makes it the source of an epithet the record uses continuously. Covered by the standing formulaic exclusions.

sharedText: and the things that I have given them shall pass
reason: The stream's top candidate for the verse and pure connective tissue. Jeremiah 8:13 is the surely-consuming of Judah's vine and fig tree; 30:3 is a book coming forth to the Gentiles and being carried to a remnant. No content word is shared, and the run consists of a relative clause and an auxiliary. The two other candidates for this verse, Ezekiel 12:28 and Exodus 32:34, are of the same kind and are covered by the same reasoning.

'From the hand of' is one of the KJV's commonest prepositional formulae and it is doing nothing here beyond joining a blessing to its giver. Psalm 106:10 saves Israel from the hand of him that hated them. The two other candidates the stream returned for this verse, 1 Samuel 6:9 and Job 2:10, are the same kind of match on 'the hand of God' and are covered here. The real borrowing at 30:6 is Acts 9:18's falling scales, which no stream proposed.

sharedText: it came to pass that the Lord
reason: The narrative formula, covered by the standing exclusion filed at 1 Nephi 2:1. Listed only because it was the sole candidate the stream returned for a verse whose actual source is Revelation 14:6, identified manually — a clean illustration of CONVENTIONS §9: the machine offered boilerplate and missed a four-item list matching one of Revelation's seven orderings exactly.

sharedText: with the fruit of his mouth
reason: The stream's second candidate for a verse whose first candidate scored 22.71 and is right. Proverbs 18:20's 'A man's belly shall be satisfied with the fruit of his mouth' shares a construction with Isaiah 11:4's 'with the rod of his mouth' and nothing else; the sense — being fed by one's own speech — is unrelated to smiting the earth. Registered because the phrase looks distinctive in isolation and is not.

sharedText: the lion shall eat straw like the
reason: The most instructive exclusion in the chapter. Isaiah 65:25 is the same vision by the same prophet — 'The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock… They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain' — and it is exactly what a writer working from memory would be expected to conflate with Isaiah 11:6-9. The Book of Mormon does not conflate them. 30:13 reads 'straw like the ox', which is Isaiah 11:7's word, where 65:25 has 'bullock'; and it keeps the cow, the bear and their young ones lying down together, which 65:25 drops entirely. The stream ranked 65:25 here and again at 30:15, and it is excluded at both on the readings rather than on rank. That the two Book of Mormon witnesses to Isaiah 11 both avoid the parallel oracle is part of the collation result argued at 30:9.

sharedText: as the waters cover the sea
reason: 'As the waters cover the sea' occurs in exactly two KJV verses, Isaiah 11:9 and Habakkuk 2:14, and Habakkuk is excluded on the clause it governs. Habakkuk reads 'the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD'; Isaiah 11:9 and 2 Nephi 30:15 both read 'the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the LORD' — 'full' not 'filled', and no 'glory of'. Two divergences in one clause, both going the same way. Registered because Habakkuk 2:14 is the more familiar form of the sentence in devotional English and is the version a reader is likelier to have by heart.

sharedText: shall be made manifest… it shall be revealed
reason: A genuine two-phrase overlap and still the wrong source. 1 Corinthians 3:13 has both 'shall be made manifest' and 'it shall be revealed', which is why the stream reached it, but its subject is every man's work tried by fire on the day of judgment, and it lacks the word the Book of Mormon's clause turns on: 'secret'. 'Nothing is secret' occurs in exactly one KJV verse, Luke 8:17, and Luke pairs 'secret' with 'made manifest' exactly as 30:17 does — where Mark 4:22 crosses the terms and Matthew 10:26 uses neither. The link is filed at Luke 8:17 with Ephesians 5:11-13 as composite for the works of darkness.

sharedText: in the light, and there is
reason: Six words of which five are function words, spanning a clause boundary in both texts. 1 John 2:10 is about abiding in the light without occasion of stumbling; 30:17's 'in the light' belongs to works of darkness being made manifest, which is Ephesians 5:13's antithesis and not John's. A textbook case of a contiguous window closing across a seam.

Five words of which four are auxiliary and preposition. Daniel 11:43 gives the king of the north power over the treasures of gold and silver of Egypt; 30:18 takes power away from Satan over the hearts of men. Only the construction is shared, and it is a common one. The verse's real source is Revelation 20:3, whose 'deceive the nations no more' occurs in exactly one KJV verse and which supplies the bounded term that 30:18 keeps while declining to say how long it is.
